# Shipyard

Shipyard is a small release-management toolkit built live during the Claude Code Bootcamp (Cohort 2).
Python 3 standard library and plain HTML/JavaScript only. No package installs.

The human who reviews and merges a change is the engineer of record. Claude proposes; the engineer of record decides.

## shipctl: release task manager

```sh
python3 shipctl.py add "Freeze public API" --owner maya --due 2026-11-05
# Added #1: Freeze public API
python3 shipctl.py add "Write release notes"
python3 shipctl.py assign 2 omar
python3 shipctl.py due 2 2026-11-02
python3 shipctl.py list                       # pending, by due date
python3 shipctl.py list --owner maya --status all
python3 shipctl.py stats
python3 shipctl.py done 1
python3 shipctl.py delete 2
```

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `add <title> [--owner O] [--due YYYY-MM-DD]` | add a release task |
| `assign <id> <owner>` | set the owner |
| `due <id> <YYYY-MM-DD>` | set the due date |
| `list [--owner O] [--status pending\|done\|all]` | list tasks (default: pending) |
| `stats` | pending, done and overdue counts per owner |
| `done <id>` | mark completed |
| `delete <id>` | delete |

Data lives in `./tasks.json`; set `SHIPCTL_DB=/path/file.json` to use another file.
Exit codes: `0` success, `1` user error, `2` storage error.

## Notes API and release dashboard

```sh
python3 seed.py                    # demo tasks + notes (use --force to reset)
python3 -m notes_api.server        # http://localhost:8000/  (PORT, NOTES_DB, SHIPCTL_DB env vars)
```

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/health` | liveness |
| `GET /api/tasks` | shipctl tasks (read-only) |
| `GET /api/notes?q=&tag=` | list, search and filter notes |
| `POST /api/notes` | create `{title, body, tags}` |
| `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/notes/{id}` | read, partial update, delete |

## Tests

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -q
node --test dashboard/tests/

# Dashboard architecture

The release dashboard is static HTML plus ES modules, served by `notes_api/server.py` next to the JSON API. No build step, no dependencies.

## Data flow

```
GET /api/tasks, /api/notes
        │
     api.js  ── fetchTasks(), fetchNotes({q, tag})   (only module that calls fetch)
        │
     app.js  ── state {tasks, notes, owner, status, q, tag}, event wiring, startup
        │
   rules.js  ── pure: filter, sort, KPIs, owners, tags, overdue
        │
   render.js ── DOM writes by element id; format.js builds safe markup strings
```

Dependencies point one way: `app.js` -> `api.js`, `render.js`; `render.js` -> `rules.js`, `format.js`. `rules.js`, `format.js` and `api.js` never touch the DOM; `render.js` never reads `state` or calls the network.

## Modules

| File | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `index.html` | Markup and element ids (the contract with `render.js` and `app.js`) |
| `styles.css` | Layout; 2×2 KPI cards and card-style rows below the mobile breakpoint |
| `app.js` | Owns `state`; wires filter, search (200 ms debounce) and tag-chip events; `init` loads data then `renderAll` |
| `api.js` | `fetchTasks`, `fetchNotes`; on any failure logs with `console.error` and returns `[]` |
| `rules.js` | `todayIso`, `isOverdue`, `filterTasks`, `computeKpis`, `uniqueOwners`, `allTags` |
| `format.js` | `escapeHtml`, `formatBody` |
| `render.js` | `renderKpis`, `renderOwnerFilter`, `renderTasks`, `renderTags`, `renderNotes`, `renderLastUpdated` |

## Behaviours to keep
- Owner and status filters re-render the task table only (client-side, no request).
- Search and tag chips reload notes from the API, then re-render notes, tag chips and KPIs in that order.
- Tasks are loaded once at startup; there is no polling or refresh.
- `app.js` starts only when `document` exists, so modules import cleanly under Node.

## Adding a feature
1. Pure logic goes in `rules.js` with a test in `dashboard/tests/`.
2. A new request goes in `api.js` with a stubbed-`fetch` test for the exact URL.
3. New markup: add the id to `index.html`, a `render*` function in `render.js` that takes data as arguments, and the call in `app.js`.

# Shipyard

Shipyard is a small release-management toolkit built live during the Claude Code Bootcamp (Cohort 2).
Python 3 standard library and plain HTML/JavaScript only. No package installs.

The human who reviews and merges a change is the engineer of record. Claude proposes; the engineer of record decides.

## shipctl: release task manager

```sh
python3 shipctl.py add "Freeze public API" --owner maya --due 2026-11-05
# Added #1: Freeze public API
python3 shipctl.py add "Write release notes"
python3 shipctl.py assign 2 omar
python3 shipctl.py due 2 2026-11-02
python3 shipctl.py list                       # pending, by due date
python3 shipctl.py list --owner maya --status all
python3 shipctl.py stats
python3 shipctl.py done 1
python3 shipctl.py delete 2
```

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `add <title> [--owner O] [--due YYYY-MM-DD]` | add a release task |
| `assign <id> <owner>` | set the owner |
| `due <id> <YYYY-MM-DD>` | set the due date |
| `list [--owner O] [--status pending\|done\|all]` | list tasks (default: pending) |
| `stats` | pending, done and overdue counts per owner |
| `done <id>` | mark completed |
| `delete <id>` | delete |

Data lives in `./tasks.json`; set `SHIPCTL_DB=/path/file.json` to use another file.
Exit codes: `0` success, `1` user error, `2` storage error.

## Notes API and release dashboard

```sh
python3 seed.py                    # demo tasks + notes (use --force to reset)
python3 -m notes_api.server        # http://localhost:8000/  (PORT, NOTES_DB, SHIPCTL_DB env vars)
```

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/health` | liveness |
| `GET /api/tasks` | shipctl tasks (read-only) |
| `GET /api/notes?q=&tag=` | list, search and filter notes |
| `POST /api/notes` | create `{title, body, tags}` |
| `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/notes/{id}` | read, partial update, delete |

## Tests

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -q
node --test dashboard/tests/
```

The dashboard is split into modules and both test suites pass, but I haven't run the browser check at 1280 px or 390 px. This machine has no Chromium, and the Python `playwright` package isn't installed, so I couldn't capture a before/after DOM or compare screenshots with the Project 7 evidence.

## What changed
- **New modules in `dashboard/`:** `rules.js`, `format.js`, `api.js` and `render.js`. `app.js` now holds only the state, event wiring and startup. The code moved as planned, with the same ids, URLs, markup and re-render order.
- **Tests:** in `dashboard/tests/app.test.mjs` only the import lines changed. I added `dashboard/tests/api.test.mjs` with 4 tests for the exact fetch URLs, the `[]` fallback on errors, and `formatBody`.
- **Docs:** I wrote `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/HANDOFF.md`, and added a dashboard layout section to `README.md`.
- **Left alone:** `index.html`, `styles.css`, the Python API, `seed.py`, `SAFETY.md`, `.claude/` and `briefs/`. Nothing is committed.

## Test output
`node --test dashboard/tests/`, last lines:
```
1..10
# tests 10
# pass 10
# fail 0
```
`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -q`:
```
Ran 46 tests in 2.826s

OK
```
Before the refactor the dashboard suite ran 6 tests, all passing. It now runs 10 because of the new API tests.

## Other checks
- `fetch(` appears only in `api.js`.
- All 13 ids used with `getElementById` are the ones already in `index.html`.
